verdict.rationale: Zapier documents a developer platform for building custom integrations. Developers can use the Visual Builder or the Platform CLI (Node.js, OAuth1/OAuth2 authentication, webhooks, polling triggers, HTTP middleware), and integration versions move through a documented lifecycle that starts in a "private" state. Partners also get a dedicated sandbox workspace. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of building a private integration with the CLI, plus deeper evidence on sharing private integrations.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom connector or private integration with a documented developer platform, SDK, or CLI

citations.quote: Zapier Platform CLI enables developers to build integrations using Node.js v22, OAuth1/OAuth2 authentication, webhooks, polling triggers, and HTTP middleware.
Build a Zapier integration - design triggers and actions for your product, wire up authentication, then publish to the App Directory.
Use the Visual Builder for quick, no-code setups or the CLI for full control and customization.
lifecycle states an integration version can go through, including private, promoted, available, legacy, deprecating, and deprecated
